s: A Baroque gate tower with a medieval memory
w: Built in 1256 as a gatehouse during Bern's second city expansion, the original tower stood for nearly four centuries before it was pulled down in 1640 and rebuilt almost immediately after - the Baroque version still standing guard on the old town's edge, protected within Bern's UNESCO World Heritage core.
_facts: Baroque tower in Bern, part of the UNESCO Old City of Bern World Heritage Site
Original tower built 1256 as a gate house during Bern's second city expansion
Demolished in 1640 and completely rebuilt immediately afterward

s: Bern's natural science collection, run with the university
w: Run in close partnership with the University of Bern, this museum draws around 131,000 visitors a year through its halls of natural science. It's the sort of institution that quietly anchors a city's scientific life - unglamorous work, done properly, for a long stretch of Bern's civic history.
_facts: Natural History Museum in Bern, Switzerland
Cooperates closely with the University of Bern in teaching and research
Visited by around 131,000 people yearly

s: The zoo that also looks after Bern's famous bears
w: Opened in 1937 on the bank of the Aare near the old town, this public zoo houses some 3,000 animals across 15 hectares - and it's the outfit responsible for the bears on show at Bern's landmark Bärengraben pit. The city owns it, funds most of it, and a staff of 27 keeps the whole menagerie running.
_facts: Public zoo in Bern, opened 1937, operated by the Tierparkverein Bern association
Owned and mostly financed by the city of Bern; on the bank of the Aare near the historic centre
Exhibits some 3,000 animals on 15 hectares; cares for the bears shown at the Bärengraben

s: Bern's best Art Nouveau, bell tower and all
w: Karl Moser raised this Reformed church between 1902 and 1905, held up as one of Switzerland's finest Art Nouveau buildings. A 36-metre tower holds five bells, stained glass by Max Laeuger glows over blue-and-green interiors, and a 2009 restoration returned its 1905 organ to the front of the nave.
_facts: Reformed church built by architect Karl Moser 1902-1905 in Art Nouveau style
One of the best examples of Art Nouveau in Switzerland, a cultural property of national significance
36m bell tower with 5 bells; stained glass by Max Laeuger; 2009 restoration returned the organ to its 1905 position

s: A fortified tower guarding Bern's oldest bridge
w: Part of the UNESCO-listed Old City, this fortified tower stands beside the Untertorbrücke, together forming one of Bern's most guarded medieval river crossings. A cultural property of national significance - a small, stubborn stronghold that's outlasted whatever it was built to defend against.
_facts: Fortified castle and tower in Bern, part of the UNESCO Old City of Bern World Heritage Site
Located together with the adjacent Untertorbrücke bridge
A Swiss cultural property of national significance

s: Where the Swiss government has run things since 1902
w: Three interconnected wings, built in stages from 1852 to 1902, house Switzerland's federal government under one roof: parliament, executive and chancellery together. The west wing solved a nineteenth-century space crisis by uniting administration and government for the first time; the National Council still meets here.
_facts: Building housing the Swiss Federal Assembly and Federal Council in Bern
West wing built 1852-1857, east wing 1884-1892, central parliament building 1894-1902
National Council and Council of States meet in the parliament building on Bundesplatz

s: 800 years of guard tower, prison and astronomical clock
w: Built in the early thirteenth century, this medieval tower has done a bit of everything - guard tower, prison, clock tower, civic memorial - and it's still Bern's oldest monument. Its fifteenth-century astronomical clock keeps drawing crowds, part of why the whole structure anchors the Old City's UNESCO listing.
_facts: Medieval tower in Bern built in the early 13th century
Served as guard tower, prison, clock tower, centre of urban life and civic memorial
Bern's oldest monument, with a 15th-century astronomical clock; heritage site of national significance

s: Switzerland's tallest cathedral took 470 years to finish
w: Construction on this Gothic Reformed minster began in 1421, but its tower - all 100.6 metres of it - wasn't finished until 1893. That makes it the tallest cathedral spire in Switzerland, and a cultural property of national significance sitting right at the heart of Bern's old city.
_facts: Swiss Reformed cathedral in the old city of Bern, Gothic style, construction began 1421
Tower completed in 1893, reaching 100.6 metres
Tallest cathedral in Switzerland; a Cultural Property of National Significance

w: Architect André Lambert modelled this 1894 building on old castles, since it was originally conceived as the Swiss National Museum - a title that went to Zurich instead. Bern kept the castle-shaped consolation prize anyway, expanded it further in 2009, and it remains the country's second-largest historical museum.
_facts: Second largest historical museum in Switzerland, designed by architect André Lambert, built 1894
Originally conceived as the Swiss National Museum before that role went to Zurich
Modelled on historic 15th and 16th century castles; extension completed 2009

s: The gallery Christo wrapped for its 50th birthday
w: Opened in 1918, this exhibition hall has hosted a startling run of avant-garde names - Klee, Giacometti, Jasper Johns, Bruce Nauman - and in 1933 gave Ernst Ludwig Kirchner his largest retrospective, curated by the artist himself. For its fiftieth anniversary, Christo and Jeanne-Claude wrapped the entire building.
_facts: Kunsthalle art exhibition hall in Bern, opened 5 October 1918
Hosted Ernst Ludwig Kirchner's largest retrospective in 1933, self-curated
Exhibited Klee, Giacometti, Henry Moore, Jasper Johns, Bruce Nauman and others; wrapped by Christo and Jeanne-Claude for its 50th anniversary

s: The Child-Eater Fountain, still at it since the 1500s
w: A painted stone fountain at Kornhausplatz showing a giant mid-bite on a sack of babies - one of the Old City's fountains dating back to the sixteenth century. Nobody's fully settled on what the figure is meant to represent, which has only helped it become one of Bern's most photographed oddities.
_facts: Painted stone fountain at Kornhausplatz in Bern, Swiss for 'Child-Eater Fountain'
One of the Old City of Bern's fountains dating from the 16th century
Part of the UNESCO Old City of Bern World Heritage Site

s: Founded on Friedrich Dürrenmatt's dying wish
w: Playwright Friedrich Dürrenmatt left his literary estate to the Swiss state on one condition: that it build a national archive for literature. It did, in 1991, and the Swiss Literary Archives now hold around 100 major and 120 partial estates across all four national languages, housed inside the Swiss National Library.
_facts: Swiss Literary Archives (SLA) in Bern, collects literary estates in German, French, Italian and Romansh
Founded 1991, part of the Swiss National Library, traced to the will of Friedrich Dürrenmatt
Holds around 100 important literary estates and about 120 partial estates and collections

s: Lady Justice, copied all over Switzerland ever since
w: The only Bernese fountain to keep every original sixteenth-century design element, its centrepiece is Hans Gieng's Lady Justice - a figure so admired it was copied across Switzerland into the mid-1600s. Vandals badly damaged the original statue in 1986; the one on Gerechtigkeitsgasse today is a faithful copy.
_facts: Gerechtigkeitsbrunnen, a 16th-century fountain in the Gerechtigkeitsgasse, Old City of Bern
Only Bernese fountain to retain all original design elements; features Hans Gieng's Lady Justice statue
Original statue largely destroyed by vandals in 1986; current statue is a copy

w: At Helvetiaplatz, this museum takes the Swiss relationship with its mountains - people, culture, nature - as its subject, with a photo archive past 220,000 images and one of the largest collections of mountain relief models anywhere. Less a shrine to peaks than an argument for how thoroughly they shaped the country.
_facts: Swiss Alpine Museum at Helvetiaplatz 4 in Bern
Focuses on the relationship between mountains and people, culture and nature in the Swiss Alps
Collection includes over 220,000 photographs and one of the largest collections of mountain relief models

s: A squatted riding school, legalised after several evictions
w: First occupied by squatters in the 1980s, this self-managed cultural centre at Neubrückstrasse 8 survived repeated eviction attempts before the city gave up and let it stay legal. Decades on, it's still Bern's loudest experiment in running an arts and social space entirely outside the usual channels.
_facts: Self-managed social centre at Neubrückstrasse 8 in Bern
First squatted in the 1980s
Legalized after several evictions
